overview: The Medford Zoning Board of Appeals is the municipal body responsible for adjudicating petitions for variances, special permits, and administrative appeals under local zoning ordinances and Massachusetts General Laws Chapters 40A and 40B. The archive's coverage spans 71 meetings from June 2022 through September 2026. Across this period, the board handled major Chapter 40B comprehensive permits, commercial developments, cannabis licensing, and a steady docket of residential dimensional relief. As of September 2026, the board is actively evaluating proposals involving newly implemented state accessory dwelling unit (ADU) regulations, while continuing to approve local residential additions, use conversions, and commercial permits.

threads.name: Chapter 40B comprehensive permits
threads.summary: The board received legal training on Chapter 40B regulations in September 2022 before opening a multi-session review of a 350-unit proposal at 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway, which it approved in July 2023 with linkage fee waivers and fire safety conditions. In late 2023, the board began evaluating a 289-unit Chapter 40B development at 970 Fellsway, ultimately granting the comprehensive permit with partial linkage fee waivers in May 2024. A separate Chapter 40B application for 378 units at 280 Mystic Avenue was introduced in April 2024 but withdrawn by the applicant in June 2024. In late 2024, the board determined that subsequent design refinements to 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway constituted insubstantial changes, and in early 2025 approved a partial demolition at 970 Fellsway to facilitate a lot split preserving open ratios.

threads.name: Cannabis dispensary permitting
threads.summary: Following a briefing on the municipal cannabis zoning ordinance, the board approved a special permit and site plan in August 2022 for Theory Wellness to operate a dispensary and arts center at 162 Mystic Avenue. In April 2023, after preliminary continuances, the board granted a special permit for New England Organics to operate a retail dispensary at 114 Mystic Avenue. In May 2026, the board approved medical sales and manufacturing special permits for Victory Gardens at 114 Mystic Avenue while continuing courier delivery requests. Delivery services for the 114 Mystic Avenue facility were subsequently approved in July 2026.

threads.name: Accessory dwelling units
threads.summary: The board began adjudicating proposals for accessory dwelling units (ADUs) in July 2026 under evolving state regulations, granting rear yard setback variances for an attached ADU addition at 621 Fulton Street. At the same meeting, hearings for attic expansions and ADUs at companion properties 1-3 Vassar Street and 12 Wellesley Street were continued to examine applicable state zoning rules. Both petitions were continued again in August 2026 and September 2026 to allow the applicant to submit reduced designs and enable the board to seek additional legal counsel.

threads.name: Administrative appeals and code enforcement
threads.summary: In February 2023, the board dismissed an appeal concerning 80 Canal Street as invalid because it was filed beyond the statutory 30-day timeline. In March 2026, the board heard an administrative appeal regarding 33 Watson Street and upheld the Building Commissioner's violation notice classifying the keeping of chickens as an illegal livestock use when a motion to overturn failed to reach a supermajority. In May 2026, the board upheld a zoning notice of violation regarding 91 Waterville Road for operating a commercial gutter business out of a residential property.

threads.name: Board governance and leadership
threads.summary: Mike Caldera was elected board chair in March 2023, serving through April 2024 when Jamie Thompson was elected chair following Caldera's resignation. Thompson resigned in early 2025, leading the board to re-elect Caldera as chair in February 2025. In March 2026, the board elected Andre Leroux as chair. Throughout these terms, the board regularly addressed member appointments, meeting times, rules and regulations updates, and the implementation of software tools to manage transcript backlogs.

threads.name: 590 Boston Avenue redevelopment
threads.summary: In July 2022, the board granted a 12-month extension for a previously approved variance and special permit to redevelop a gas station at 590 Boston Avenue into a 40-unit mixed-use building. After further short-term extensions, the board in November 2023 approved amendments increasing the unit count from 40 to 45 and reconfiguring parking to an at-grade design. The board granted an additional six-month extension in January 2024 to allow the developer to maintain its permits through July 2024.

threads.name: Residential conversions and multi-family zoning
threads.summary: The board routinely heard petitions seeking to create or expand multi-family residential structures, approving a conversion of commercial space to apartments at 20-22 High Street in September 2022 and granting variances for a three-family conversion at 12 George Street in April 2023. A four-unit addition to a historic dwelling at 54 South Street was contested and withdrawn before being approved with revised setbacks in August 2023. Recent cases include the conversion of an auto repair station into three townhouses at 85 Elm Street in early 2025, variances for a two-family conversion on an undersized lot at 121 Second Street in August 2025, and use variances to erect second single-family homes on oversized lots in 2026.

periods.narrative: The board navigated citywide zoning recodification, adjudicated cannabis dispensary applications, and conducted an extensive multi-month review to approve a 350-unit Chapter 40B comprehensive permit on Mystic Valley Parkway.

Proceedings were dominated by the comprehensive review and approval of the 289-unit Chapter 40B development at 970 Fellsway, leadership transitions, and steady dockets of residential dimensional variances and special permits.

Under new leadership, the board resolved contested administrative enforcement appeals, granted expanded cannabis delivery and commercial permits, and began interpreting new state regulations regarding accessory dwelling units.
